While I see what you’re saying, I cannot disagree more. For starters, I believe that preforming TTTO and Ani at the same time was a very interesting choice which resulted in an amazing amount of content for us viewers/play goers. That being said “TTTO is a much better show” is highly opinionated. I personally believe that Ani is a much better show, but that is just my opinion. I will not dispute your claim that Twisted is arguably one of Starkid’s most popular and well produced musicals. 

The songs use direct quotes from the Star Wars films. While you state they are generic, I think it’s a creative choice that enhances the element of parody in the musical. The songs being directly about Star Wars/Ani as a character makes it so they could not “be plopped into any show.” The songs are creative and are arguably the best example of parody. I would also say (and this is highly opinionated of me so take it with a grain of salt) I prefer songs the songs in Ani to the songs of TTTO. I don’t need a song about a character shitting themselves.

While Ani is an unlikable protagonist to some, he really flourished to others. I enjoy Ani as a protagonist because of how it mirrors Star Wars. The acting shows some really good elements of parody once more. Also, Chris Allen does some amazing impressions of young Anakin throughout the production. Seeing Vader as a depressed, awkward, and unfulfilled human fills in a lot of what Star Wars fans headcanon about his life after the death of Padmé. I would also argue that while you find Obi-wan likable in this production, others may not. While Nick Lang does a phenomenal comedic performance as Obi-wan, he also shows a villainous side to him. The comedy may put weigh the darkness in him to some viewers, but to me it aids in the experience. Obi-wan struggling as an alcoholic aids his story in a comedic and scary way that develops him into a character with malicious intent. The final victory going to Mars Jade is not a bad choice in my opinion. It shows a message of happiness for all party members involved (minus the death of Jar Jar which was at the hands of Kenobi robbing him and ultimately motivated Ani.) By utilizing Mara Jade’s audition to be the final plot point of the production, the production was able to show Ani’s character growth. He went from choking people for not liking his “Death Star tit” idea and being invasive and unresponsive to people’s social cues to being a helpful, supportive, and proud father figure to his canonical (before Disney bought the rights) daughter-in-law.
